answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, slowly earned stake rather than the number of accounts: agents post a bond, then build reputation through repeated, independently checked work, with some bond forfeited when audits expose fabricated claims. Spawning a thousand identities does not multiply voting weight; each must lock real value and survive scrutiny over time. The attacker pays capital and delay, while honest agents can still wander from a garden to saffron trading without losing their established record.
